title: perf-bench-scratch-devon-brooks-2026-03-26
content:
Goal:
Quick scratchpad for KV-cache + batching perf runs (compare A100 vs H100, baseline vs kv-cache, different batch sizes / concurrency). Purpose: pick default batching and cache settings for MPT-7B-v1 serving profile for interactive chat (typical seq_len 256) and long-context eval (seq_len 1024).

Notes / config used: 
- Model: mpt-7b-v1 (float16 / q4f16 experiments later)
- Runtime build: rt-2026-03-20 (kernel selection changes applied)
- HW: 1xA100-80GB (driver 525), 1xH100-80GB (driver 535) -- isolated node, no noisy neighbors
- Batcher: continuous batching; explicit batch_size param used to cap max on GPU (1,4,8)
- Concurrency: per-client concurrency set to 1,4,8 (we run single-worker bench with grpc client driving concurrent requests)
- KV-cache: enabled (prefix caching) vs disabled. Cache warmup: for cache-enabled, warm with 100 requests of similar prompt prefixes before measuring.
- Seq lengths: 256 (chat), 1024 (long context)
- Prompt / workload: 50 unique prompts sampled from prod prompt set (mix of instruction + context), generation length: 128 tokens
- Metrics: p50, p95 (total response latency), tokens/sec (end-to-end measured by client), GPU utilization (nvidia-smi sampling), observed memory usage (max RSS on process)

Run summary (cleaned):

A) Seq_len=256, batch_size=1 (no compaction), concurrency=1
- A100 baseline (no kv): p50 120ms, p95 210ms, tokens/sec 340
- A100 kv-cache: p50 95ms, p95 165ms, tokens/sec 420
- H100 baseline: p50 80ms, p95 140ms, tokens/sec 620
- H100 kv-cache: p50 65ms, p95 110ms, tokens/sec 760

B) Seq_len=256, batch_size=4, concurrency=4 (aggressive batching)
- A100 baseline: p50 240ms, p95 450ms, tokens/sec 980 (higher throughput but latency worse)
- A100 kv-cache: p50 200ms, p95 380ms, tokens/sec 1180
- H100 baseline: p50 160ms, p95 300ms, tokens/sec 1500
- H100 kv-cache: p50 135ms, p95 260ms, tokens/sec 1820

C) Seq_len=1024, batch_size=1, concurrency=1
- A100 baseline: p50 540ms, p95 920ms, tokens/sec 120
- A100 kv-cache: p50 420ms, p95 760ms, tokens/sec 150
- H100 baseline: p50 360ms, p95 620ms, tokens/sec 220
- H100 kv-cache: p50 300ms, p95 520ms, tokens/sec 270

D) Seq_len=1024, batch_size=4, concurrency=4
- A100 baseline: p50 1700ms, p95 2600ms, tokens/sec 360
- A100 kv-cache: p50 1400ms, p95 2100ms, tokens/sec 420
- H100 baseline: p50 1200ms, p95 1900ms, tokens/sec 540
- H100 kv-cache: p50 980ms, p95 1600ms, tokens/sec 660

Observations / quick takeaways:
- H100 consistently outperforms A100 across latency and throughput for these configs. For interactive low-latency settings (seq_len 256, batch 1), H100 gives ~1.8x tokens/sec vs A100.
- KV-cache yields measurable latency improvements across the board (roughly 15-25% p50 reduction for seq256, slightly larger for long context with repeated prefixes). Benefit is larger when there's prefix reuse (expected).
- Batching increases throughput but at cost of p95 latency; for interactive use we should keep max_batch_size=4 and prefer concurrency controls to avoid large latency spikes.
- For long-context (1024) workloads, kv-cache still helps but memory pressure increases; observed GPU memory usage on H100 + kv-cache peaked ~72GB for batch_size=4 -> OK but close to limits for multi-tenant.
- Kernel-selection improvements in rt-2026-03-20 appear to reduce tail latency on H100 (compare to older run from last week where p95 was ~10% higher).

Raw sample logs (trimmed):
- [2026-03-25T14:02:11Z] run_id=rb-256-b1-a100-kv-001; p50=95ms; p95=165ms; tps=420; gpu_mem_max=56GB; util=73%
- [2026-03-25T14:10:03Z] run_id=rb-1024-b4-h100-nokv-004; p50=1200ms; p95=1900ms; tps=540; gpu_mem_max=78GB; util=88%

Notes on noise and validity:
- Made sure no other pods on node during runs. Network overhead small (client ran on same VPC).
- For fairness, used same model weights and same runtime build across HW; libcuda + cuDNN versions differ (H100 environment is newer) — might account for small differences; record drivers above.
- Randomness: runs repeated 3x, numbers above are median of runs.

Recommended defaults for interactive hosted API (based on perf + cost tradeoffs):
- default_max_batch_size: 4 (helps throughput for bursty traffic without extreme tail latency)
- default_concurrency_per_worker: 4 (lets batching kick in; enforce request-level client concurrency limits per tenant in control plane)
- enable_prefix_kv_cache: true (on by default for chat-type endpoints where prefix reuse common)
- memory_safety_margin: 5GB reservation on H100 nodes for safekeeping auto-scale buffers

Next actions / TODOs:
- Run q4f16 quantization profile for mpt-7b (expect lower mem + similar latency) — target: 2026-03-29
- Add colder-start bench (cache cold, compile warm) and measure compile-time overhead separately — ticket JIRA-INF-2357
- Run multi-tenant bench: 4 clients across 4 models to validate memory isolation and eviction heuristics
- Pull GPU counters (nvprof or CUPTI) to better understand kernel-level hotspots for seq1024 workloads
- Sync with runtime team on kernel selection heuristics change in PR #412 (Sam to drive follow-up)

Notes-to-self: keep these rough logs in Drive; once we have q4f16 numbers, assemble a short deck for product and SRE with recommendation and estimated cost delta for hosted API tiers.

End of scratchpad.
